# 2 Baruch Chapter 9 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Syriac MS (Codex Ambrosianus 7a1) | **Section:** The Fall of Jerusalem

---

**1** I, Baruch, went and sat before the temple gate, weeping and mourning. I cried out: "Lord, why did you burn your own vineyard? Why did you devastate your own land? Why did you allow the garden you planted with your own hand to be destroyed?

**2** Every prophet left among your people is now being taken into exile. There is no one left here to comfort me, your servant."

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic rendering. "Garden you planted with your own hand" for "plantation of your right hand" — more vivid. The final line personalizes the lament ("comfort me, your servant"), emphasizing Baruch's isolation.*
